antimetabolite drugs inhibit clonal expansion of T cells whereas lymphoablative agents inactivate differentiated T cells.
contact hypersensitivity can be prevented during the sensitization phase by drugs that inhibit cell proliferation and during the elicitation phase by drugs that kill effector T cells.

the immunosuppressive antimicrotubule drugs, cyclosporin and tacrolimus, inhibit the expression of contact hypersensitivity whereas the antimetabolites, methotrexates and mycophenolate, inhibit its induction.

the development and application of new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of contact hypersensitivity.
the development of immunosuppressive therapies that can be applied to the control of skin diseases.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induction and the expression of contact hypersensitivity are two different and distinct processes.
the immunosuppressive antimicrotubules inhibit the induction of the reaction whereas the immunodepletive drugs inhibit the expression.
the immunosuppressive antimatabolites inhibit induction of the contact hypersensitivity response whereas the lymphoablative agents inhibit expression of the contact hypersensitive reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
contact hypersensitivity is a T cell dependent reaction that requires T cell proliferation for sensitization but not for expression.
contact hypersensitivity requires clonal expansion but not proliferation of T cells for its expression.

antimetabolite drugs inhibit contact hypersensitivity when given during sensitization but not challenge, whereas lymphoablative agents inhibit contact hypersensitivity during both sensitization and challenge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunosuppressive and lymphoablative agents have different effects on the induction of contact hypersensibility and that the time of administration is a crucial factor.
immunosuppressive antimicrobial drugs are useful in preventing contact hypersensitivity while immunosuppressive lymphoablative agents are useful in treating established contact hypersensitivity.
contact hypersensitivity is not a T cell dependent phenomenon and that immunosuppressive therapy should be administered during sensitization rather than during the elicitation phase.
